Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

Before implementing the upgrade action economy changes, we need unit tests that verify the action-spend behavior for all three upgrade paths. These tests will fail initially (red) and pass after implementation (green), providing regression coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test move-to-hand action cost: `moveToHandCommand` for upgrade cards calls `consumeAction()` and decrements `actionsRemaining`. Test that when `actionsRemaining <= 0`, the command fails with appropriate legality error.
- Test same-day composite free: When an upgrade was moved to hand same-turn via `moveToHandCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand` does NOT consume a second action (same-day composite). Test verifies `actionsRemaining` unchanged after play.
- Test held-card play costs action: When an upgrade was held from a previous day (not same-day), `playUpgradeFromHandCommand` consumes 1 action. Test verifies `actionsRemaining` decremented.
- Test drag-drop premium: `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand` consumes 1 action and charges the +50% premium (`Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`). Test verifies both action cost and premium amount.
- Test legality gating: All upgrade paths reject when `actionsRemaining <= 0`. Test covers click path, hand-play path, and drag-drop path.
- Test free ops unchanged: Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free (no action consumed); refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- Existing unit tests pass: All existing tests in `tests/main-street/` continue to pass.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `buyUpgradeCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`, `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `executeAction` action handling
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-action-economy.test.ts` — new test file

## Problem statement

`npm run monte-carlo` (and `monte-carlo-sweep`) fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because `tsx` does not understand Vite's `?raw` query suffix used to import `card-data.csv` in `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Users

- **TCE developer** running Monte Carlo balance analysis: expects `npm run monte-carlo` to produce `results/main-street-monte-carlo.json` and `.csv`.
- **CI/automated tooling** (future): may run the harness headlessly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo -- --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --strategy greedy --out results/main-street-monte-carlo.json --csv-out results/main-street-monte-carlo.csv` completes successfully (exit 0) and produces valid output files.
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep -- --sweep --seeds 100 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --out results/sweep.json --csv-out results/sweep.csv` completes successfully (exit 0).
3. `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript + Vite production build).
4. Full test suite `npm test` passes.

## Constraints

- The fix should use `vite-node` (already proven to work; documented in `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67).
- Per the Doc-Update Policy, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` scripts list must be updated if scripts change.
- Do not modify `tsx` or add loader hooks — that is more fragile and less established.

## Existing state

- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` imports Main Street game code which uses `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw';`
- `package.json` defines `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` scripts using `tsx`.
- `vite-node` works for the same import (used by `scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`).

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` npm scripts in `package.json` from `tsx` to `vite-node`. Update documentation (DEVELOPER.md, AGENTS.md) to reflect the change.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Change `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` script commands.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update script listings to reflect `vite-node` usage.
- `AGENTS.md` — Update scripts list to reflect `vite-node` usage.

## Related work

- Discovered from: CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW (Monte Carlo sanity check)
- Sibling pattern: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 documents `vite-node` usage for a similar import path.
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1-F4 work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Why not fix tsx instead of switching to vite-node?" — Answer: tsx does not support Vite `?raw` queries natively; adding a loader hook is fragile and unmaintainable. vite-node is the established pattern in this repo (see `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`). Source: code review of `MainStreetCards.ts` and `card-catalog.md`.
- Q: "Are there other `tsx` scripts that might also break on `?raw` imports?" — Answer: No — `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `scripts/replay.ts` and `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` are the only scripts using `tsx`. The `export-transcripts.ts` does not import Main Street code. `replay.ts` may import Main Street but does not import `?raw` CSV. Source: grep of `scripts/` for `tsx` and `?raw`.

# Intake Brief: Main Street: npm run monte-carlo (tsx) fails on ?raw CSV imports

## Headline

`npm run monte-carlo` fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because tsx cannot load the Vite-style `card-data.csv?raw` import; switch the affected npm scripts from tsx to vite-node (the verified, in-repo-precedented runner) and update docs per the Doc-Update Policy.

## Problem statement

Three npm scripts that transitively import `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, `save-load-smoke`) fail under tsx with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. tsx's loader misparses the Vite `?raw` query suffix for non-TS/TXT extensions, treating the CSV as a JS module. Root cause is in the import chain (`MainStreetCards.ts` line 18: `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`), not in the harness logic — the same harness runs correctly under vite-node.

## Users

- **Developer running balance validation** — "I want `npm run monte-carlo` to just work so I can verify card balance after rebalancing card-data.csv." Example story: after editing `card-data.csv`, a developer runs `npm run monte-carlo` (or `monte-carlo-sweep`) and gets the JSON + CSV outputs described in docs.
- **Developer running the save/load smoke check** — "I want `npm run save-load-smoke` to pass so I can quickly verify persistence round-trips." Currently it crashes with the same loader error before running any scenario.
- **Producer/CI reader** — wants the documented commands in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` to remain accurate and working.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo` completes successfully end-to-end with the default settings (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, greedy, maxTurns 25) and writes both JSON and CSV outputs; results are consistent with the verified working control run (200/200 runs; winRate 38.5%, medianScore 55.8, avgNoActionTurns 0 — i.e., determinism preserved, no balance drift).
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep` completes successfully in sweep mode (strategy × difficulty combinations) and writes its outputs.
3. `npm run save-load-smoke` completes successfully (exit 0, failures 0) — same root cause, same fix; expanded blast radius captured in this item.
4. Spot-check that unaffected tsx workflows still work (`npm run replay` or `balance-cards`) — no collateral regression from the runner switch.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, AGENTS.md scripts list, and docs/DEVELOPER.md, per the Doc-Update Policy; the vite-node rationale is documented in the same style as `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- The npm script **names and CLI flags must not change** (`npm run monte-carlo`, `--seeds/--seed-prefix/--maxTurns/--strategy/--out/--csv-out`, `--sweep`, etc.) — the harness CLI is a documented interface.
- Testing/validation criterion preserved: seeded determinism must be maintained (same seed → same deal order → same outputs; no reliance on RNG ordering changes).
- Prefer the established runner pattern over bespoke tooling: **vite-node** is the in-repo precedent for scripts that import `MainStreetCards.ts` (see `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` already uses it for exactly this reason) and is verified working for both broken entry points. A custom tsx loader hook for `?raw` would work but is more complex, repo-specific, and has no precedent — evaluated and rejected as the primary path.
- Doc-Update Policy applies (package.json scripts change).

## Existing state

- `package.json` lines 17–18, 21: `monte-carlo` / `monte-carlo-sweep` = `tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts ...`; `save-load-smoke` = `tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` line 18 imports `./card-data.csv?raw` (Vite bundler syntax, docs comment: "bundled at build time via Vite's `?raw`").
- Import chains that break under tsx: `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` → `MainStreetMonteCarlo` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`; `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`.
- Reproduced failures: `npx tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `npx tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` both exit 1 with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` (Node v22.22.1).
- Verified working: `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/monte-carlo.ts --seeds 200 ...` (200/200; winRate 38.5%) and `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` (failures 0).
- Tests are unaffected — vitest handles `?raw` via Vite (e.g. `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`).
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b (before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1–F4) and at HEAD.

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, and `save-load-smoke` package.json scripts from `tsx` to `vite-node` (entry scripts stay unchanged). Update docs per the Doc-Update Policy (AGENTS.md scripts list, docs/DEVELOPER.md; add the vite-node rationale for MainStreetCards-importing scripts in the same style as card-catalog.md). No engine or game code changes expected.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — scripts lines 17–18 (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`) and 21 (`save-load-smoke`): tsx → vite-node.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — root cause location (`import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`); likely unchanged, but should be re-verified and its "bundled at build time" comment cross-referenced.
- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` — entry points; unchanged, but verification targets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (lines ~197, ~230), `AGENTS.md` (scripts list, line ~76) — doc updates per Doc-Update Policy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) — precedent/template for documenting the vite-node rationale.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY — DUPLICATE** (status open): identical description, created 7 seconds earlier — a double-submit of this item. Producer to resolve (likely close in favour of this item, CG-0MT4RBHQR006C5GR).
- CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW — "Monte Carlo sanity-check and full-suite verification" (open, in_progress): the discovering item; this bug was found while verifying it. `discovered-from` relationship already recorded.
- CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA — "Main Street: reputation score multiplier" (in_progress, plan_complete): commit b2bec26b predates this work; bug reproduced before and after it (pre-existing, not a regression of that item).
- CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY — "Replay CLI tests ... (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm ...)" (completed): related tsx CLI tooling context.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — documents the vite-node precedent for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (approach):** vite-node is the chosen fix over a tsx `?raw` loader hook — based on in-repo precedent (card-catalog.md), verified success on both broken scripts, and lower maintenance surface. If the producer prefers the loader-hook approach, scope is limited to the monte-carlo/save-load-smoke invocations and the doc updates shrink accordingly.
- **Assumption (scope):** fixing `save-load-smoke` in the same item is in-scope — same root cause, same fix, verified working under vite-node. If the producer wants to split it, create a child item.
- **Risk:** switching runners could subtly change module resolution for other `@alias` imports in the chain — mitigated by the verification ACs (output parity with the control run; full test suite) and by the existing precedent (vite-node already used for a MainStreetCards-importing generator).
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to harness logic, balance logic, or CSV handling are in scope; any balance-tuning opportunities surfaced by the working harness are separate work items (see CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Intake investigation (herdr-downtime) — findings and clarifying questions**

## Investigation summary

- **Root cause:** `biz-florist` had `baseIncome=0` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` at report time (2026-08-23) — a 5-cost business with zero income, zero rep, and no synergy bonuses. A genuine defect.
- **Fix already landed on dev:** commit `257c6298` (2026-08-24), part of completed work item CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE ("rebalance Main Street economy for business ongoing costs (income raise + tiered rep)"), raised the Florist to `baseIncome=3.0`, `reputationPerTurn=0.1`, `ongoingCost=1.25`. Current `dev` HEAD `828d72e7` (2026-08-29) includes it.
- **Runtime verification (current dev):** placing a Florist solo → `computeBusinessIncome = 3.0`/turn, rep +0.1/turn; synergy rate defaults to 0.5 (most bridge cards have empty `synergyCoinBonus`; not florist-specific). CSV column alignment verified (33/33).
- **Residual gaps found (not yet addressed anywhere):**
  1. No regression test locks business template incomes — the only Florist test (`tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts`) checks synergy types only; `baseIncome > 0` is not asserted template-wide. `balance-cards.test.ts` skips cards with falsy `baseIncome`.
  2. Stale doc: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md:236` still cites Florist as an example of a "zero base income" card.
  3. Pre-fix checkpoint saves would still load florist `baseIncome=0` (`MainStreetCards.loadTemplatesFromCsv` deliberately trusts saved checkpoint CSV over bundled data).

## Clarifying questions (need producer answers before the brief can be finalised)

1. **Reproduction basis:** Was the "provides no income" observation from a game/save started before 2026-08-24 (pre-rebalance)? Current dev appears fixed (3.0/turn, verified). Is there any still-reproducible symptom on current dev — or is the fix sufficient?
2. **Scope if fixed:** Accept the scope: add a regression test asserting every business template has `baseIncome > 0` (excluding intentional rep-only cards such as Clinic), fix the stale doc reference in `prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md`, then close this item as already-fixed? Or is a re-balance/redesign of the Florist preferred instead?
3. **Legacy saves:** For pre-fix checkpoint saves, should the engine migrate/override the saved florist income, or is "start a new game" the acceptable path (current by-design behaviour)?
